work_item: B04 connect existing bidirectional CSV and JSON table conversions to the normal Core route
source_snapshot_method: SHA-256 of the compact JSON file inventory in code-snapshot.json

tests_and_route.reason_not_executed: This continuation did not request test or runtime-route verification; only formatting, compilation, lint and build checks were run.

implemented_routes: apps/cli -> Core::run -> input::structured_intent -> Intent::CsvToJson -> document::csv_to_json -> DocumentResult artifact
apps/cli -> Core::run -> input::structured_intent -> Intent::JsonToCsv -> document::json_to_csv -> DocumentResult artifact
existing_component_observation: At base commit e724316, csv_to_json and json_to_csv existed as pure document functions but had no ordinary Core intent consumers.
supported_behavior_from_source: CSV-to-JSON requires a header-mode declaration: English `csv-to-json header:` / `csv-to-json no-header:` or the corresponding explicit Japanese header.
CSV-to-JSON produces the strict string-table schema {"columns":[string,...] | null,"rows":[[string,...],...]}; numeric-looking text is never converted to a JSON number.
JSON-to-CSV accepts the strict columns/rows table schema with string cells, rejects unknown or duplicate fields and invalid structure, writes CRLF records and rejects formula-leading cells.

Both transformations return DocumentResult data with source/output digests, parameters and source/output byte spans. Core stores that record as an artifact dependency and exposes only the transformed text as the result content.
Input body bytes are retained after the directive newline; explicit grammar failures stay unresolved, and the functions impose bounded source/output size, rows, columns and cell counts.
This route does not write a user-selected filesystem path; the converted result is a Core-managed artifact. No source-data truth or general schema-transformation claim is made.
